original_client: Social Wars 0.02a SWF under Ruffle + original Flask server
static_source_clue: IsoFightingElement.acquireNewTarget defaults to max(Config.AGGRO_RANGE, iAttackRange). This is distinct from confirmed runtime aggro radius. IsoUnit.IA_Attack moves towards target when distance > iAttackRange.
conclusions: In this fixed north-vector scenario, automatic kill persisted at starting distances 5, 10 and 15.
At 15 tiles, the attacker moved five map tiles persistently before the enemy disappeared.
At 20 tiles, no native kill and no persisted movement were observed for 25.339 s of post-modal control sampling.
This is consistent with an acquisition/engagement boundary somewhere between 15 and 20 for the selected layout, but it is not a measured global threshold.
uncertainties: For killed scenarios, enemy was already removed before the first of the two control samples, so time-to-first-attack was not isolated.
At 20 tiles the enemy was outside the captured camera frame, so visual inaction cannot be independently confirmed from screenshot.
Distance is tile Manhattan distance only, not pathfinding distance or obstacle-aware line-of-sight.
No response within 25.339 s is not proof enemy cannot ever be reached or targeted.
The original client's terrain/visibility and scripted encounter rules may affect target acquisition.
No independently recompiled client has been demonstrated.
